decisions.approvalNote: User retained Option 1 and explicitly expanded it with Context Browser naming, Data Management conversion handoffs, Dataset Preparation-style ordered extraction and chunking, source-grounded topic and summary generation, and manual context entry. The user clarified that already processed means already chunked, so chunk reuse requires authoritative persisted chunk records and lineage rather than generic prepared-dataset status.
decisions.context: The repository has workspace-scoped artifacts, reusable Dataset Preparation parsing and chunking modules, managed local text-generation and embedding runtimes, and shared ordered workflow components, but no context-management domain or vector-store dependency. The selection must preserve clean Data Management handoffs, bounded source-grounded generation, cross-host parity, and portable saved context without silently broadening trust or credential boundaries.

consequences: The Manage navigation gains Context and Home gains a Context card on desktop and thin client.

Data Management artifact details expose Convert to RAG database only for locally readable supported textual, structured-text, tabular, or document artifacts, and pass only a one-time workspace-bound artifact reference rather than content.
RAG and context-pack tabs mirror Dataset Preparation with Add data, Check data, Prepare context, and Review and create steps using shared workflow and source-selection presentation.

Textual datasets open with their artifact selected. Persisted chunks are reused only after the application boundary validates their source digest and exact row, field, page, or region lineage; prepared datasets without those records still show compatible fields for confirmation and proceed through RAG chunk extraction.
Context packs can combine authorized sources and manual context, preview extracted topics and source-grounded summaries with citations, and require explicit review before materialization.

Context Browser manages saved outputs, source freshness, exact Data Management source links, rebuild/delete actions, and bounded retrieval testing; Artifact Browser still lists the underlying materialized artifacts.
Vectors, raw chunks, manual text, prompts, and model payloads remain out of general artifact metadata and AssetAiContext.
options.label: Data-linked Embedded Context Studio
options.summary: Build a shared workspace-scoped Context page with RAG Databases, Markdown Context Packs, and Context Browser tabs. Both generators use the Dataset Preparation four-step ordered pipeline and shared source-processing capabilities. Eligible textual artifact detail dialogs open the RAG tab with the exact artifact preselected and recognize it as already chunked only when persisted chunk records and exact lineage are authoritatively validated. RAG creates a portable SQLite database artifact. Context packs accept artifacts and/or bounded manual context, then perform source-grounded core-topic extraction and constrained summarization with explicit model/method selection, citations, review, Save, and Discard.
tradeoffs: Delivers a coherent two-way Data Management and Context experience without a separately operated vector service or new production credential boundary.

Requires shared handoff contracts, authoritative chunk-record inspection, reusable normalization/chunking boundaries, constrained topic/summary generation, exact lineage, host transports, and cross-host workflow UI rather than a page-only change.
Uses existing SQLite, transformer, constrained-output, artifact, and workflow capabilities; no vector-database dependency is planned.
Bounded cosine retrieval is appropriate for local and small-to-medium collections; a later adapter is needed for very large corpora.

Model-assisted summaries require explicit readiness, prompt-injection controls, citations, and review; deterministic extractive processing remains available and a selected unavailable AI mode never silently falls back.

consequences: Data Management and Context UX remains linked, but saved RAG context is a local manifest plus a remote collection rather than a self-contained artifact.
The roadmap requires a separate provider choice, secure credential configuration, operations documentation, cross-tenant denial testing, and controlled-environment qualification.
The first delivery is larger and unavailable when the vector service cannot be reached.
options.label: Data-linked external service
options.summary: Build the same Data Management handoffs, ordered generation workflows, source/manual context-pack generation, and Context Browser, but use a managed external vector service as the first RAG backing while retaining only a local manifest artifact.
tradeoffs: Scales indexing and retrieval beyond an embedded bounded scan.
Adds deployment, health, network egress, credentials, tenancy, retention, deletion, backup, provider versioning, and offline behavior before the basic workflow can work.
Reduces portability and makes local desktop development dependent on external infrastructure unless a second embedded adapter is also implemented.

consequences: Manage navigation and Home still gain Context, but the page contains only RAG Databases and Markdown Context Packs tabs.
Saved outputs and their source linkage are visible only through generic Artifact Browser details.
A later roadmap is required for context-specific browsing, stale-source detection, rebuilding, and retrieval testing.
options.label: Linked generation-only artifacts
options.summary: Add the two ordered generators and Data Management Convert to RAG database handoff, save embedded RAG and Markdown artifacts, and use the existing Artifact Browser for all post-save management.
tradeoffs: Smaller initial Context-specific management surface while preserving the requested source handoff and generation capabilities.
Avoids Context Browser freshness, rebuild, deletion, and retrieval-test reads in the first implementation.
Leaves users without a context-specific way to validate retrieval quality, inspect source-grounded summaries, or manage stale context.

constraints: Add a workspace-required Context page to desktop and thin-client Manage navigation and add a Context card to both Home surfaces.
Provide RAG Databases, Markdown Context Packs, and Context Browser tabs with shared host-neutral behavior and host-specific desktop IPC/preload and thin-client API clients.

Use the same four-step ordered pipeline and shared WorkflowSequence/WorkflowStep, sectioned panel, readable checkbox, status, advanced-setting, and final-action presentation conventions as Dataset Preparation without importing feature-local host code across boundaries.

Add Convert to RAG database to eligible Artifact Browser View Details modals, pass only a one-time active-workspace artifact identifier, and validate local availability, source type, fields, version, digest, and any persisted chunk records and lineage authoritatively after navigation.
Provide reverse links from Context Browser source citations to exact Data Management artifact details and clear stale handoffs or selections when workspace scope changes.

Reuse Dataset Preparation media capability, document normalization, tabular/structured extraction, and chunking semantics through a neutral shared boundary; do not fork parsers or weaken existing Dataset Preparation behavior.
Allow context-pack input from authorized artifacts, bounded manual context, or both; distinguish authored, extracted, and generated content and retain exact digests and citations.

Support deterministic extractive and explicitly selected constrained local-model core-topic and summary generation; fail closed when the selected method or model is unavailable or malformed and never silently substitute methods.

Treat saved RAG databases and Markdown packs as materialized workspace artifacts with bounded safe manifests and catalog visibility; keep vectors, raw chunks, manual text, source payloads, prompts, and provider/model payloads out of general metadata and AssetAiContext.
Use readable source selection, field confirmation, explicit configuration, per-chunk authoritative progress and cancellation, bounded preview/review, and explicit Save or Discard.

Propagate authoritative workspace and optional organization scope through navigation state, UI, transport, application, runtime, storage, catalog, retrieval, deletion, and source-backlink boundaries; fail closed when scope or authority is missing.

Bound source count and bytes, manual text, fields, parsed records, chunks, overlap, topics, summaries, prompts, model output, embedding dimensions, output size, query size, results, duration, polling, and retained tasks.

Treat all artifact/manual content as untrusted data rather than instructions; constrain and cite model output, render Markdown/topics/summaries/excerpts inertly, and preserve human review before save.

Expose only sanitized public diagnostics and aggregate progress; never return or log local paths, raw embeddings, protected prompts, manual/source payloads, secrets, stack traces, or raw provider/model errors.
Preserve existing dirty worktree changes and avoid coupling this roadmap to unrelated dashboard test cleanup.

Update the context ADR, architecture and threat-model docs, Data Management and security context packs/routing, affected host and module READMEs, and all cross-host linkage and regression tests in the same change.
Run focused tests while iterating, then documentation, architecture, agent-support, server/thin-client build, standard, end-to-end, AI, and all-suite gates at each completed increment boundary.

Manual text, source content, prompts, model output, vectors, paths, secrets, or stack traces leak through navigation state, metadata, diagnostics, notifications, logs, or browser detail.

Crafted names, storage keys, archive members, Markdown, links, citations, or retrieval excerpts escape approved boundaries or execute active content.
Cancelled, discarded, failed, or workspace-switched generation leaves orphaned databases, ZIPs, vectors, manual drafts, tasks, catalog records, or stale selection state.

Reuse allowlisted Data Management media capabilities and bounded neutral parsers/chunkers, normalize safe names, confirm text fields for any source without valid persisted chunks, use artifact-owned keys, and accept no caller-controlled physical paths.

Treat artifact and manual content as inert untrusted data; offer deterministic extractive processing or explicit constrained local-model processing, disable tools/network access, require bounded schema-valid output and exact citations, and never silently fall back between methods.

Render names, Markdown, topics, summaries, links, citations, and excerpts as inert escaped content with constrained links, and make generated versus authored versus extracted provenance visible.

The embedded database option is optimized for bounded local and small-to-medium collections; very large corpora may require a future external adapter and controlled performance qualification.

discovery.summary: The repository already provides workspace-scoped artifact storage and detail modals, Dataset Preparation source-format capability contracts, reusable Python document normalization and Markdown chunking modules, constrained local text generation, generic cancellable runtime tasks, shared four-step WorkflowSequence presentation, and parallel desktop/thin-client routing. acceptanceCriteria.description: Contracts normalize safe names and media types, distinguish artifact and manual sources, bind handoffs to one workspace and exact artifact identity, validate persisted chunk records, source digest, and exact lineage at the application boundary before reuse, and enforce explicit bounds for source bytes, fields, manual text, chunks, overlap, topics, summaries, prompts, model output, previews, embedding dimensions, and artifact size.

RAG and context-pack generation accept the same supported textual, structured-text, tabular, and text-extractable document formats as Dataset Preparation, reuse neutral normalization/chunking code, preserve source/row/field/page lineage, reuse only authoritatively valid saved chunks, infer compatible text fields for unchunked datasets, and leave Dataset Preparation output unchanged under regression tests.

One-to-four synthetic raw, unchunked dataset, and already-chunked sources generate a valid bounded SQLite RAG database with stable chunks, exact citations, recorded embedding configuration, progress after every completed chunk, cancellation, and sanitized failure behavior; valid chunks are reused and all other sources are chunked.

Artifact sources, bounded manual context, and their combination generate a valid Markdown context-pack ZIP whose manifest distinguishes authored, extracted, and generated content and whose preview contains bounded core topics and source-grounded summaries with exact citations; deterministic and explicitly selected constrained-model methods never silently substitute for one another.

Successful generation remains staged until explicit Save or Discard; Save atomically verifies and catalogs the selected output under the authorized workspace, while Discard, cancellation, workspace change, and injected partial failures leave no staged bytes or catalog orphans.

Configured compatible embedding and local text-generation models complete one tiny RAG build and one tiny topic/summary context-pack build through the managed runtime without exposing cache paths, manual content, prompts, vectors, or raw model/runtime payloads.

Missing or mismatched workspace/organization scope, forged handoffs, inaccessible or stale sources, false already-chunked hints, absent or invalid chunk lineage, unsupported formats, unsafe names, excessive manual text or source sizes, invalid field/chunk settings, source prompt injection, malformed constrained model output, unavailable selected models, cancellation races, and storage failures fail closed with bounded sanitized diagnostics and no silent fallback.
